Another example is "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers".

He also wrote in and translated from English and French.
Bhabani Bhattacharya | Bhabani Bhattacharya (10 November 1906–10 October 1988) was an Indian writer, of Bengali origin, who wrote social-realist fiction.  He was born in Bhagalpur, part of the Bengal Presidency in British India.  Bhattacharya gained a bachelor's degree from Patna University and a doctorate from the University of London.  He returned to India and joined the diplomatic service.  Bhattacharya served in the United States, to which country he returned as a teacher of literary studies once he had left the service.  He taught in Hawaii, and later in Seattle.  In his mid-thirties Bhattacharya began writing fiction set in historically and socially realistic contexts.
